transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's gotten really bad. I'll be working, and just one saw starting up in the shop, or somebody walking past, or even just a random thought about another job... it completely pulls me off whatever I’m doing. And then before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me.
Have you had this kind of trouble focusing since you were a child?

Yeah, I have. Even back in grade school, definitely before I was twelve. I remember my teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright kid, but just... careless. I was always losing my homework, or I'd completely forget the instructions they just gave us. I'd just end up staring out the window instead of actually finishing my seatwork.
Do these focus problems also cause trouble for you outside of work, like at home or in daily life?

Yeah, it really does. At home, my husband has basically had to take over all the bills and reminders. I just keep misplacing important papers, or I'll completely miss what needs to get done around the house. 

And honestly, it's hurting me at work more than ever, too. The mistakes and delays have actually cost me commissions, and I've had to do rework on jobs because I messed something up. It's gotten to the point where the rest of the crew is a lot less willing to rely on me for things like scheduling or ordering materials. It's just really frustrating.
Do you find yourself getting distracted in situations outside of work and home too, like during conversations or errands?

Well, I guess... I mean, mostly it's just work and home that I notice it. If I'm out running errands, I usually have a list my husband made, so I just kind of stick to that. And with conversations... I don't know, I haven't really thought about it. Maybe sometimes I drift a little if it's a long story, but I wouldn't say it's a huge problem like it is at the shop or with the bills. It's really just those main areas where it's causing all the trouble.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get pretty frustrated with myself when I mess up at the shop or lose important papers, but I'm not feeling down or depressed all day. It's really just the annoyance of not being able to keep things straight, but my mood itself is mostly fine.
Besides work and home, do you also have trouble paying attention in other settings, like social situations?

Well, like I was saying before, I don't really notice it much outside of work and home. Socially... I guess I'm okay. I might drift a bit if someone's talking for a long time, but I wouldn't say I have real trouble paying attention when I'm out with friends or anything. It's mainly just the shop and the house where things get messy.
Do you often find that worry makes it hard for you to concentrate?

Not really. I don't think I'm much of a worrier. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting there stressing about things and that's why I lose track of what I'm doing. My mind just sort of... wanders off on its own, even if I'm perfectly calm. Like I said, I get pretty annoyed with myself after I mess up a measurement at the shop or lose a piece of paper, but worry isn't what's causing the distraction in the first place.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really impulsive like that. I don't just blurt things out or jump into things without thinking. It's really just the focus and keeping track of things that I struggle with, not acting without thinking.
Have you ever been through something very frightening or traumatic that still makes you feel on guard?
No, I haven't. I've had a pretty normal life in that regard. Nothing traumatic or overly frightening has happened to me, and I definitely don't walk around feeling on guard or anything like that.
